observation: In the first actual model tool run, the storage query missed, a refined query found the answer, and three pulls failed before one succeeded. The model used a record UUID as receipt_id, then a handle UUID, then an index request UUID. The eventual answer was correct and cited the pulled source. No-memory produced malformed tool-call text; it is not a clean answer baseline.
intervention: Show each existing index entry with one complete pull_command composed from its actual receipt and version-matched handle. Keep summary, record/version, body digest, class/kind, mandatory bootstrap and session limits. Raw canonical responses remain in the private host log. All authority and live checks remain in the unchanged server.
prospective_observations: source UUID corresponds to successful full-body pull
number and error codes of failed pulls
total tool calls and model requests
limits: One additional trial on an already-used development question. Differences may include stochastic model behavior, different UUIDs, provider routing and latency. Fewer errors in this run would support this presentation choice, not establish a general or causal advantage. Retain original failures; do not rerun the no-memory arm until it happens to pass.
production_scope: Experimental tool adapter presentation only. No core API, ranker, credential, storage or recovery change. Broader packaging for real harnesses requires its own usage and contract checks.
